proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof (the construction of W_j and C_Ω), stated for a general measure μ.

1. Put m := c • μ.restrict(Ω × G). A Varifold N n Ω consists of four fields: openness of Ω, a measure, the support condition m(Ωᶜ × G) = 0, and finiteness m(K × G) ≠ ∞ for every compact K ⊆ Ω. Openness of Ω is a hypothesis.

2. (Support condition.) Ω is open, so Ωᶜ × G is Borel. Since (Ωᶜ × G) ∩ (Ω × G) = ∅, Measure.restrict_apply gives μ.restrict(Ω × G)(Ωᶜ × G) = μ(∅) = 0. Hence m(Ωᶜ × G) = c·0 = 0 (Measure.smul_apply, smul_zero).

3. (Finiteness on compact sets.) Let K ⊆ Ω be compact. Then m(K × G) = c·μ.restrict(Ω × G)(K × G). Measure.restrict_apply_le, which holds for every set, gives μ.restrict(Ω × G)(K × G) ≤ μ(K × G), and μ(K × G) ≠ ∞ by hypothesis. Since c ≠ ∞, the product is finite (ENNReal.mul_ne_top), so m(K × G) ≠ ∞.

4. Hence W := ⟨Ω open, m, step 2, step 3⟩ is a Varifold N n Ω, and W.measure = m = c • μ.restrict(Ω × G) holds by definition (rfl). ∎
key_steps: m(Ωᶜ × G) = c·μ(∅) = 0 by Measure.restrict_apply, since Ωᶜ × G is Borel.
For compact K ⊆ Ω: m(K × G) ≤ c·μ(K × G) < ∞ (restrict_apply_le, c ≠ ∞).
Package these as a Varifold N n Ω; its measure is m by rfl.
